The '''2023 ATP Masters 1000''' season is the thirty-fourth edition of the [[ATP 1000]] Series tennis tournaments. The champion of each ATP 1000 event is awarded 1,000 rankings points.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Emma |date=2022-08-09 |title=This is the ATP calendar of 2023 |url=https://www.p1travel.com/blog/atp-calendar-2023/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/20221107183334/https://www.p1travel.com/blog/atp-calendar-2023/ |archive-date=2022-11-07 |access-date= |website=P1}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Rohit |date=16 November 2022 |title=Tennis Schedule 2023: Complete ATP and WTA tennis tour calendar for 2022-23 |url=https://www.sportskeeda.com/tennis/tennis-schedule-2023-complete-atp-wta-tennis-tour-calendar-2022-23 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221201232208/https://www.sportskeeda.com/tennis/tennis-schedule-2023-complete-atp-wta-tennis-tour-calendar-2022-23 |archive-date=2022-12-01 |access-date= |website=www.sportskeeda.com |language=en-us}}</ref>

Beginning this year, the ATP 1000 events in Madrid, Rome, and Shanghai were expanded to two weeks in duration with a 96-player draw for singles.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Ramchandani |first1=Haresh |title=Tennis: ATP Tour announces expanded format for 5 more Masters events |url=https://www.tennismajors.com/atp/five-more-atp-masters-1000-events-to-move-to-96-player-draws-as-part-of-atp-tour-onevision-plan-605654.html |website=Tennis Majors |access-date=7 October 2023 |date=10 June 2022}}</ref>

Russian and Belarus players competed under no nationality due to the [[2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine|Russian invasion of Ukraine]].
